name: Named Entity Consistency
description: Evaluates the stability and contextual coherence of named entities (people, organizations, locations, specialized terminology) throughout a text. While AI models can convincingly introduce entities, they frequently struggle with long-range dependency, resulting in 'entity drift' where the attributes, roles, or relationships of a specific entity subtly warp or contradict themselves later in the document.
algorithm: Cross-Document Entity Coreference and Attribute Verification
mechanism: The system utilizes advanced Named Entity Recognition (NER) to extract and index all distinct entities (e.g., 'Dr. Smith', 'GlobalCorp', 'Protocol X'). It then builds a localized knowledge graph connecting these entities to their associated verbs, adjectives, and contextual roles across the entire document. The algorithm scans for 'hallucinatory contradictions'—instances where the AI forgets the established constraints of an entity. For example, indicating that a person died in chapter two but quoting them in chapter five, or stating a company was founded in 1990 but later describing its involvement in a 1980s event. Human writers maintain a coherent internal mental model of the entities they discuss, ensuring logical continuity even in long texts. LLMs, governed by sliding context windows and probabilistic next-token generation, lack true working memory, often prioritizing immediate localized fluency over macroscopic entity consistency.
useCase: Crucial for auditing long-form generated content (reports, biographies, research summaries, narrative fiction), where the AI is forced to juggle multiple characters, organizations, or factual data points over an extended word count.
strengths:
• Directly targets the 'hallucination' and 'context window forgetting' vulnerabilities inherent in all current autoregressive language models.
• Highly effective in exposing AI-generated fake news, fabricated case studies, or deeply flawed academic summaries.
• Provides concrete, interpretable evidence (e.g., 'Entity A is described as X on line 12, but Y on line 84').
limitations:
• Computationally expensive as it requires building internal knowledge graphs and performing cross-sentence dependency parsing.
• Can flag human-written texts that intentionally feature unreliable narrators, surrealism, or simply contain poor editing and factual human errors.
• Effectiveness drops on very short texts where there is insufficient length for entity drift to occur.
parameters:
Analysis: NER Extraction and Contextual Graph Neural Networks
Metric: Pairwise Attribute Conflict and Temporal/Spatial Contradictions
Output: 0-100 Entity Coherence (Hallucination Probability Score)
accuracy: High — 82-89% accuracy on documents exceeding 1,000 words. It is one of the most robust semantic indicators of AI generation, as it evaluates logical breakdown rather than mere statistical word choice.
